subject: Re: Structured Output Reliability — JSON schema & retry patterns
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Structured Output Reliability — JSON schema & retry patterns

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about Acme's document ingestion pipeline and how you want to use structured output for your QA/triage flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of needs you shared:
- Canonical output format for the triage API: strict JSON with a couple of optional fields (category, confidence, remediation_steps).
- High reliability requirement: failures must be retried and validated before write-to-prod.
- Embeddings and reranker used downstream for similarity / deduping; latency targets are 300–500ms p90 per request.
- Auth: will need SSO + service keys for server-to-server integration.

What we (Redwood) will provide / follow-ups: 
1) Draft JSON schema for the canonical response (attached: acme_schema_req_v1.json). This includes required fields and enum constraints for category.
2) Structured output reliability doc (attached: redwood-structured-output-guidelines.pdf) — covers constrained decoding, token-level validation, and suggested retry/backoff patterns.
3) SDK integration snippets for Node/Python showing auth, routing, and how to wire constrained-decoding + validation hooks.
4) Technical deep-dive: propose a 60-min session with our infra engineer Dev Patel and runtime lead Dylan Brooks to walk through the schema, validation checks, and embedding/reranker integration.

Proposed times for the technical session this week:
- Tue May 12, 10:00–11:00 PT
- Wed May 13, 13:00–14:00 PT

Please confirm which slot works (or share alternatives). Also call out any additional fields you need in the schema, and if you can share a small sample payload (anonymized) we can iterate quickly.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0118

(attachment: redwood-structured-output-guidelines.pdf)
(attachment: acme_schema_req_v1.json)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@acme.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Structured Output Reliability — JSON schema & retry patterns

Thanks Marissa — appreciated. Quick notes from our side after reviewing the attachments: 

- Schema: the enum for category looks good, but we need a free-text "notes" field (max 2048 chars) and an optional "source_document_id" (string). Can you add those to v1?
- Retry patterns: can you clarify what you recommend for validation failures vs model decoding errors? We want to avoid double-writes if a record partially validates.
- Embeddings/reranker: we'll be using a vector store (Pinecone) and need to confirm how Redwood recommends batching embeddings and whether we should run reranker synchronously or asynchronously given the latency target.

We're available for the Wed May 13 slot (13:00 PT). Also, in advance of the tech call, can you share:
1) A short Node SDK snippet showing how to call with constrained decoding + a validation hook
2) Your recommended JSON schema validation library (server-side) and sample validation error payloads

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson | Senior Product Manager, Search
Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com | +1 206-555-0199

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@acme.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Structured Output Reliability — JSON schema & retry patterns

Perfect — Wed 13:00 PT confirmed. Thanks for the clarifications on retries vs validation handling; that approach matches our risk model.

One last ask before the call: can you confirm whether Redwood recommends running the reranker synchronously in the request path (adds ~80–120ms) or asynchronously as a post-process with a compensating dedupe pass? We can sync on the call but wanted to flag it so Dylan/Dev can be prepared.

Also attaching our SSO integration doc and the internal procurement contact for contract redlines.

— Alex

(attachment: acme_sso_integration.pdf)
